With the sample's pom, every Java edit under `mn:dev` failed with `invalid flag: -J-Dmicronaut.data.sql.dialect-options.oracle.version=23.1`, and the stale application kept serving. The pom needs `<fork>true</fork>`, where `-J` is valid for javac's launcher. The embedded compiler calls the compiler API in the running JVM, which refuses it.

## Fix

`-J-Dkey=value` means a system property for javac's JVM, which is what annotation processors read, so dropping it would hide a real difference. The sample's generated Oracle repositories lose `SqlQueryConfiguration` without it.

`JavacJvmOptions` separates the `-J` options:
- **System properties** are set around the compilation and restored when it ends, however it ends. One embedded compilation runs at a time, so that none sees another's properties.
- **Any other `-J` option**, such as `-J-Xmx`, cannot apply to a running JVM. It is dropped with one warning that names it and the consequence.

### Why not something cleaner

- **`-A` options:** Micronaut's visitors read them first, but javac refuses a key with a hyphen, and `dialect-options` has one. A processor may also read the property directly.
- **Isolated class loaders:** the processors already load in their own, but `System.getProperty` is JVM-wide, so that doesn't scope it.
- **Mutating the properties around processing:** this is what `ProcessorOptionsSystemProperties` already does for `-Amicronaut.*`, so it is the same mechanism with the same window. While a compilation runs, a thread of the running application could read one of these keys. No context starts in that window, because the restart follows the compilation on the same thread.

## Checked against the build tool

On the sample, after a compile-all by the embedded compiler, through both plugins with the unmodified build files:

- 173 class files differ as bytes from the build tool's.
- With debug tables and constant-pool numbering set aside, only the edited class differs.
- 22 of 22 Oracle repository definitions name `SqlQueryConfiguration`, as the build tool's do.

The 173 come from `-g`: both build tools pass it and neither plugin puts it in the manifest, so embedded classes have no `LocalVariableTable`. That's a separate gap, not addressed here.

## Tests

`JavacSourceCompilerSpec` adds these cases, and the first two failed before the fix with `invalid flag`:
- a processor reads the property during the compilation, and the JVM has its old values afterwards, including after a failed compilation
- `-J-Xmx64m` warns once over two compilations
- parsing of each `-J` form

`:micronaut-dev:test` (444 tests, 1 skipped) and `:micronaut-dev-tck:test` (6) pass. `checkstyleMain` and `spotlessCheck` pass. `checkstyleTest` is skipped by the build.

## End to end

Java petclinic through `./gradlew mnDev` and `mvn mn:dev`, on H2, with the sample's own pom and Gradle build including their `-J` and `forkOptions.jvmArgs`. All three fixes were in together (serde, credited sources, forked JVM options) on the module PRs of the earlier test.

30 edits of each kind, each checked by a request. Medians are of the last 20, in ms.

| Edit | Earlier, Gradle / Maven | Gradle now (load 5) | Maven now (load 9) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| method body | 1022 / 988 | 922 | 978 |
| body in a `@Serdeable` class | exited (prototype 4444 / 4066) | 4123 | 4923 |
| compile-all from a private constant | exited (prototype 4408 / 4045) | 4129 | 4720 |
| repository query | failed on the second edit (prototype 2686 / 2423) | 2414 | 2866 |
| route | 1190 / 1118 | 1183 | 1300 |

The earlier fix series ran at load 8.2 (Gradle) and 4.0 (Maven); the prototype series at load 9 and 5.

- No exit, no failed reload, no edit left unserved. Each run kept one connection pool across its 150 edits.
- Three cycles of deleting a used DTO each gave a 503 naming the compile failure. Restoring it served `/vets/json` in 4.0-4.9 s, and a body, query and route edit after each restore all worked.
- A background checker saw 452 of 452 OK under Gradle and 439 of 451 under Maven. The 12 failures are all `ClassFormatError: Truncated class file` in JTE's first render, the JTE race the earlier test found. They are not from this work.


## Needs from the others

Nothing to merge first. micronaut-projects/micronaut-gradle-plugin#1406 passes `forkOptions.jvmArgs` as `-J` options and needs this first. The Maven plugin already writes them and needs no change.

The core is correct: properties are restored in `finally`, also after a failed compile; the static lock serialises embedded compilations; and the parser test covers `-J-D`, `-J-D=bad` and a bare `-J`. Two points:

1. **`-J--add-exports` and `-J--add-opens` are dropped** (`JavacJvmOptions` around line 64), with only a warning that the output "may differ". Builds that fork javac for Error Prone, and some Lombok setups, pass exactly these flags. Unless the dev JVM was itself launched with them, the plugin then fails with `IllegalAccessError` on every edit. Please recognise these options, check them against the running JVM's module layer, and tell the user to add them to the dev JVM's arguments.

2. **Properties the JDK reads only at startup are treated as honoured** (`JavacJvmOptions` around lines 69 and 89). `-J-Dfile.encoding` and `-J-Duser.language` have no effect in a running JVM but get no warning, while the application's global property is still changed for the length of the compile. issue.title: Compile what other modules of the build produce into a directory of its own under development mode
issue.body:
Replaces #14328, rebuilt as the bottom of a stack (`stack/dev-compile/01-sibling-output`, same commits, head c1493cc915) so that the pull requests stacked on it get CI. The body is that of #14328.

Stack #14340 on 5.3.x, bottom to top: #14331 → #14332 → #14333 → #14334 → #14335 → #14336 → #14337 → #14338 → #14339.

Part of micronaut-projects/micronaut-core#13654. Needed by the Maven and Gradle plugin PRs that write the new manifest keys.

## What was wrong

In a multi-module build the launcher compiled the sources of the modules the application depends on into the application's own class output (`target/classes`, `build/classes/java/main`). Those classes stayed there after the session. A later `mvn package` or `gradle assemble` without `clean` put them in the application's JAR, older than the source:

- Maven: `original-app-0.1.jar` held `jq/lib/Greeter.class`, `jq/lib/$Greeter$Definition.class` and the `META-INF/micronaut` entry. The source said `edited after dev`, and `java -jar` answered `edited`.
- Gradle: the same through a real `mnDev`: `app-0.1.jar` held the same three entries, and the packaged application answered `edited`.
- The next `mn:dev` or `mnDev` session on the same tree also served the stale class, because the application's output is read first. The source said `second session`, and it answered `edited`.

## The fix

Two new manifest keys, written by the plugins:

```properties
micronaut.dev.compile.sibling-sources=../library/src/main/java
micronaut.dev.compile.sibling-output=target/micronaut-dev/siblings
```

- **Routing.** There is still one compiler run, so no extra javac start. After it, `StagedSourceCompiler` moves what belongs to a sibling's source out of staging, using what it already knows: the compiler's credit by source, then the file name (`$Foo$Definition.class` and its `META-INF/micronaut` entry go with `Foo`). Classes and resources go under `<sibling-output>/classes`, generated sources under `<sibling-output>/generated-sources-<language>`. A file with no known owner goes to the sibling output when any sibling source compiled, and to the application's output otherwise. In that second case any copy in the sibling output is removed so it can't shadow the new one.
- **Reading.** `DevManifest.reloadableRoots()` puts `<sibling-output>/classes` ahead of the application's and the siblings' outputs, behind the tests' in test mode. The generation loader, the output snapshot and `InPlaceUpdates` all read that list, so they need no change of their own. Each compiler reads the directory ahead of the compile classpath, Kotlin through its filtered view. `ClassDependencyIndex` and test selection cover it too. Test compilations read it and never write to it.
- **Kotlin.** The module metadata is split, so each output lists the top-level declarations it holds. A full compilation rewrites both outputs' lists, so an output whose last top-level declaration went keeps no list of the old ones.
- **Stale state.** `SiblingOutput.prepare()` empties the directory when a launcher starts, whatever ended the last session, because the build tool has just compiled the modules. It keeps the directory in two cases:
  - Another development process holds a share of it, as `mnTest` beside `mnDev` does. This is a file lock, so `kill -9` releases it.
  - The launcher is the relaunch of a process that spent its generation budget. That process leaves a mark, valid for 2 minutes.
- **Locking.** The directory is covered by the existing `OutputLock`, whose location does not change.
- **Compatibility.** A manifest without both keys behaves as before: same roots, same outputs. An older core ignores the keys.
- **Python.** A manifest with Python sources also behaves as if the keys were absent, because the Python compiler writes only to its class output. The keys are then not read at all, and a debug log says they are ignored. No plugin writes both today.
- **Safety check.** A sibling output that overlaps the project directory, a source, resource or test root, a class, test or generated-sources output, or a sibling's source directory is refused, because the launcher empties it.
- **Class loaders.** The share a process holds is kept in a static map of `SiblingOutput`, per class loader. The launcher's classes are loaded once by the JVM's application class loader, which is never collected, so the share lasts as long as the JVM; the Javadoc of the map says so.

Nothing is added to a runtime call site.

## Tests

- `SiblingOutputSpec`, `SiblingOutputTest` and `DevManifestSpec` cover:
  - routing of classes, bean definitions, resources and generated sources, in Java, Groovy and Kotlin
  - classes compiled implicitly from the source path
  - class path order, deletion and failed compilations
  - emptying and keeping the directory, and the relaunch mark
  - another process holding a share, in a child JVM, and another runtime of the same JVM
  - a relaunch through a real launcher, with this JVM's share released in between as the end of the process would, and a launch after it that starts from the build output
  - a restart and a hot swap of a sibling's body through a real launcher
  - test selection in test mode
- `:micronaut-dev:test` ran twice on this work:
  - The first run, three commits before this head, had 469 tests, 1 skipped and no failures.
  - The run on this head had 1 failure out of 470, `ConcurrentRuntimesTest`: its probe reported a test run with `cancelled=true`. That test sets no sibling keys, and it then passed 3 of 3 runs alone.
- `checkstyleMain`, `checkstyleTest` and `spotlessCheck` pass.

## End to end

Real `mvn mn:dev` and `./gradlew mnDev` on a two-module project: edit the sibling, stop, edit again, package without clean, list the JAR, run it, then start a new session.

| | Stop | Sibling classes in the application's JAR | The package answers (source: `edited after dev`) | New session answers (source: `second session`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Maven, before | SIGTERM | 3 entries | `edited` | `edited` |
| Maven, before | kill -9 | 3 entries | `edited` | `edited` |
| Maven, after | SIGTERM | 0 | `edited after dev` | `second session` |
| Maven, after | kill -9 | 0 | `edited after dev` | `second session` |
| Gradle, before | SIGTERM | 3 entries | `edited` | not run |
| Gradle, before | kill -9 | 3 entries | `edited` | `edited` |
| Gradle, after | SIGTERM | 0 | `edited after dev` | `second session` |
| Gradle, after | kill -9 | 0 | `edited after dev` | `second session` |

`mn:dev` beside `mn:test`, and `mnDev` beside `mnTest`, both worked: the directory was not emptied when the second session started, both saw each edit, and the first kept working after the second stopped. In build-tool mode no key is written and no directory is created.

## Reload time

Edit to served, in ms, median with p10 and p90. Two-module project with 10 beans in each module. Sessions were alternated with the order reversed halfway: 4 sessions per variant, 35 rounds each, the first 10 discarded, so n=100. Load ranged from 3.7 to 10.

| | Maven before | Maven after | Gradle before | Gradle after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| sibling body (hot swap) | 375 (362, 440) | 386 (370, 478) | 408 (392, 507) | 408 (393, 505) |
| sibling structure (restart) | 395 (380, 465) | 409 (388, 527) | 440 (416, 520) | 442 (418, 541) |
| application body (hot swap) | 372 (357, 403) | 380 (363, 488) | 400 (381, 451) | 398 (379, 490) |

Gradle shows no difference. Maven's medians are 8 to 14 ms higher, and 3 to 5 ms in its closest-loaded pair of sessions. I can't separate that from load.

## Left as it was

- A sibling class that the build compiled and that is then deleted during a session still loads from the sibling's own build output until the next build. The route still answered 200 after the deletion, both before and after this change.
- The dependency index does not read a sibling's build output, so a sibling's class is not recompiled for a change in a class it references until it has been compiled here once. The launcher logs showed the same compile counts before and after in the timing series.
- Sibling test sources still compile into the project's test output.



## Review follow-up (9 Nov 2026)

- `refuseOverlap` also checks resource roots, test source roots and their outputs and generated sources, the default generated-sources directories, and the `sibling-sources` entries (tests fail before for each).
- A full Kotlin compilation no longer leaves an outdated `siblings/classes/META-INF/main.kotlin_module`: both outputs' module files are merged as the incremental path does, with every part counted as replaced (`SiblingOutputSpec`, fails before).
- `SiblingOutputTest.theRelaunchedProcessStartsFromWhat…` releases the share between the two launches, so it fails with the relaunch mark ignored. The cross-process branch (`tryLock() == null`) is covered by a child JVM holding the lock; the same-JVM spec stays for the `OverlappingFileLockException` branch. Both were checked by mutation.
- A debug log when Python sources turn the feature off; the keys are then not parsed (Codex finding).
- `origin/5.3.x` merged in.

Ran: `:micronaut-dev:test --tests 'io.micronaut.dev.compile.*'` with `DevManifestSpec` and `SiblingOutputTest`, `checkstyleMain` and `spotlessCheck` on `micronaut-dev`; the whole `:micronaut-dev:test` and `:micronaut-dev-tck:test` on the top of the stack. Codex review: one finding (parsing ignored keys), fixed.

comment.body:
## Review

The design is sound and the description matches the code. Routing, cleanup of stale state and classpath order all hold up when traced through `StagedSourceCompiler`, `DevManifest` and the three compilers. Before merging I'd fix the first point below, because it guards a recursive delete.

1. **`DevManifest.refuseOverlap` (around line 842) is narrower than the description says.** It checks only the main source roots and outputs. Anything under `projectDir` is accepted unless it overlaps one of those: resource roots, test source roots, test outputs, and `sibling-sources` entries not also in `sources.<kind>`. If a plugin bug or a hand-edited manifest sets `sibling-output=src/main/resources/x` or `src/test/java`, the check passes and `prepare()` runs `deleteRecursively` on it at every launch. Please add those directories to `others`.

2. **A full Kotlin compile leaves an outdated `main.kotlin_module`** (`KotlinSourceCompiler` around line 99, with `KotlinModuleMapping.splitInto`). On a full compile, `splitInto` returns early when no sibling part is left, and `mergeInto` is skipped, so `siblings/classes/META-INF/main.kotlin_module` from earlier in the session stays. Example: remove a sibling's last top-level function, then run a full compile. The sibling output is read first and still lists a facade such as `lib/UtilKt` that no longer exists. The incremental path handles this in `mergeInto`'s `dropped` branch.

3. **`SiblingOutputTest.theRelaunchedProcessStartsFromWhat…` cannot fail.** The "relaunched" launcher runs in the same JVM and nothing calls `release()`, so `SiblingOutput.claim()` finds the directory in `CLAIMED` whether or not the relaunch mark exists. The test still passes with `takeRelaunchMark()` removed. `SiblingOutputSpec` covers the mark properly at unit level. Similarly, the "kept while another process uses it" spec holds the lock from the same JVM, so it exercises the `OverlappingFileLockException` branch, not the cross-process `tryLock() == null` one.

4. **Minor:**
   - `CLAIMED` is static, so each class loader that loads `SiblingOutput` has its own copy. If the old loader is collected, its channel's cleaner releases the lock while a newer runtime still uses the directory. This depends on how the launcher is loaded.
   - Turning the feature off when Python sources are present is silent. A debug log would help.
   - The branch is behind `5.3.x`.

issue.title: Development mode: compile every source of an output generated from several sources
issue.body:
Replaces #14329, rebuilt in the stack on `stack/dev-compile/01-sibling-output`: the commits of #14329 merged with it, the conflict in `StagedSourceCompiler.java` (imports) and the test processors' service file resolved by keeping both sides. The body is that of #14329.

Stack #14340 on 5.3.x, bottom to top: #14331 → #14332 → #14333 → #14334 → #14335 → #14336 → #14337 → #14338 → #14339.

Found by the end-to-end test of Java petclinic through `mnDev` and `mn:dev`, part of micronaut-projects/micronaut-core#13654.

## Problem

The second edit to a repository interface took the application down with a 503, and every later edit failed too, until someone edited `H2Repositories.java`.

## Cause

A generated output is credited to every source it originates from. `H2Repositories` nests `interface H2VetRepository extends VetRepository`, so its generated classes are credited to `VetRepository.java` as well, and the mapping records `H2Repositories` for `VetRepository.java`.

When `VetRepository.java` compiles, all of its recorded classes go, `H2Repositories` and everything generated for it included. But `H2Repositories.java` was not compiled, for two reasons:
- `SourceIndex` kept one source per class, whichever the directory walk found first, so `H2Repositories` could map to `VetRepository.java`.
- As a class of the changed source, it counts as the source's own, and `transitiveDependentsOf` leaves those out.

The first edit works only because the build tool's compile left no mapping.

The shape is wider than repositories. With Micronaut's real processors, a bean that inherits injection points from a project superclass is credited to the superclass's source too, so editing that superclass removed the subclass's classes and its bean. KSP credits the same way.

I also checked `@Import` and `@Introspected(classes = ...)`. Both name what they generate after the annotated class, with one credit, so they are not affected.

## Fix

The rule is now that an output that goes must be written again by every source that can write it:
- `SourceIndex` knows every source of a class, with the source its path names first.
- For javac, selection follows every source that shares a class, generated source or resource with one selected or deleted, until nothing new turns up. A class compiled from a generated source is credited to all of that source's origins.
- For KSP, whose processors keep state and rewrite what they aggregate themselves, only the source a class belongs to is added. KSP's `ALL_FILES` credit every source, so following them would compile everything on every edit.

## Cost

A source that shares no output compiles alone, as before, and a test asserts it. On petclinic a repository edit now compiles 17 sources rather than the 8 the prototype compiled, because every repository interface shares the generated holders.

On petclinic that costs no measurable time: a repository edit serves in 2414 ms with Gradle at load 5, and 2468 ms with Maven at load 7, against 2686 and 2423 on the prototype, which ran at load 9 and 5.

The same applies to subclasses of a project base class with injection points: editing one subclass compiles its siblings too. For example, when every controller extends a base class with `@Inject` fields, each `$X$Definition` is credited to the base class's source, so editing one controller compiles all of them. The group has no size limit, and the petclinic numbers don't measure this shape. A debug log of `StagedSourceCompiler` gives the size of each such group (`N source(s) share an output with the M selected and D deleted: a group of G source(s) compiles together`). Narrowing it would need telling an input of a generated class from a producer of it, and the filer doesn't say which is which.

## Known gaps

Both come from having no recorded credit to follow, and both only affect a processor that aggregates over several sources, such as the `finishCompilation` beans of micronaut-projects/micronaut-core#14294:
- A new or restored source joining an aggregate compiles alone the first time, so the aggregate is written from that source until any member compiles again. A test records the recovery.
- The first edit after a build tool's compile has no mapping, so the same applies.

#14294 is not merged. I tested this shape with a test processor, not with that PR.

## Tests

`JavacSourceCompilerSpec` adds these cases, and the first three failed before the fix:
- a nested bean credited to its interface, edited twice
- a bean inheriting injection points
- an aggregate of a source and a resource, through edit, delete and restore
- a source sharing nothing, which compiles alone

`KotlinSourceCompilerSpec` adds the inherited bean under KSP, which also failed before the fix.

`:micronaut-dev:test` (446 tests, 1 skipped) and `:micronaut-dev-tck:test` (6) pass. `checkstyleMain` and `spotlessCheck` pass. `checkstyleTest` is skipped by the build.

## End to end

Java petclinic through `./gradlew mnDev` and `mvn mn:dev`, on H2, with the sample's own pom and Gradle build including their `-J` and `forkOptions.jvmArgs`. All three fixes were in together (serde, credited sources, forked JVM options) on the module PRs of the earlier test.

30 edits of each kind, each checked by a request. Medians are of the last 20, in ms.

| Edit | Earlier, Gradle / Maven | Gradle now (load 5) | Maven now (load 9) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| method body | 1022 / 988 | 922 | 978 |
| body in a `@Serdeable` class | exited (prototype 4444 / 4066) | 4123 | 4923 |
| compile-all from a private constant | exited (prototype 4408 / 4045) | 4129 | 4720 |
| repository query | failed on the second edit (prototype 2686 / 2423) | 2414 | 2866 |
| route | 1190 / 1118 | 1183 | 1300 |

The earlier fix series ran at load 8.2 (Gradle) and 4.0 (Maven); the prototype series at load 9 and 5.

- No exit, no failed reload, no edit left unserved. Each run kept one connection pool across its 150 edits.
- Three cycles of deleting a used DTO each gave a 503 naming the compile failure. Restoring it served `/vets/json` in 4.0-4.9 s, and a body, query and route edit after each restore all worked.
- A background checker saw 452 of 452 OK under Gradle and 439 of 451 under Maven. The 12 failures are all `ClassFormatError: Truncated class file` in JTE's first render, the JTE race the earlier test found. They are not from this work.


## Needs from the others

Nothing to merge first. It conflicts lightly with the sibling-output work in `StagedSourceCompiler.java` and the test processors' service file.



## Review follow-up (9 Nov 2026)

- Debug log of the group size, no cap. Test: three beans extending a base class with an injection point; editing one compiles all four sources and logs the group (the log assertion fails before).
- Codex review: the log miscounted a group seeded by deleted sources; it now names the deleted ones separately.

Ran: `:micronaut-dev:test --tests 'io.micronaut.dev.compile.*'` with `DevManifestSpec` and `SiblingOutputTest`, `checkstyleMain` and `spotlessCheck` on `micronaut-dev`.

comment.body:
## Review

The logic is correct and the description's claims hold:
- `SourceIndex.scan` keeps every source of a class, with the class's own file first.
- The worklist in `selectSources` is transitive, starts from both selected and deleted sources, and adds only files that exist.
- `produced()` credits a class compiled from a generated source to every source that generated it.
- Stale credits fix themselves, because sharing is symmetric.

One design point: for javac, any shared credit or shared resource joins sources into one group that always compiles together, and the group size has no limit. For example, in an app where every controller extends a project base class with `@Inject` fields, each `$X$Definition` is credited to `Base.java`, so editing one controller compiles all of them. The PR states the cost, but the petclinic numbers don't measure this shape. A debug log of the group size, or a cap, would make it visible.

The restore gap the PR lists is real and the test records it: after a restore, the aggregate is written again from the restored source alone.
